item.title: American Samoa Is Resisting US Plan to Mine Nearby Seabed
item.description: About 32 million acres of South Pacific seabed off American Samoa could be auctioned in November in what would be the world’s first competitive lease sale for offshore critical minerals. The winning bidders would secure the rights to develop the zone’s minerals over a 20-year term. The US Department of Interior’s Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), ... Read more

item.title: Protecting Earth’s fragile biodiversity takes spotlight at Armenia talks
item.description: Biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people whose future prosperity depends on countries taking urgent action to protect our planet, the top UN official leading talks at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, said on Monday.

item.title: Guterres honours Indonesian troops who paid ‘ultimate sacrifice’
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.

item.title: Gaza: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
item.description: Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

item.title: UN condemns deadly wave of drone strikes in war-torn Sudan
item.description: Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.

item.title: Hunger is ‘an avoidable tragedy’ in a world of plenty: Türk
item.description: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food, even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday, blaming injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.

item.title: Haiti: Elections on hold as gangs adapt to security crackdown, Security Council hears
item.description: Armed groups in Haiti are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas, the UN warned the Security Council on Monday.

item.title: ‘Season of fear’: Escalating Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers, deadly strikes on Gaza
item.description: Israeli attacks on war-torn Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year-old ceasefire agreement. Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, settler violence continued through the ongoing olive harvest, with UN independent experts on Monday urging Israel to protect Palestinian farmers.
